entities.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of the singular verb וַיַּרְא. It names the God who saw the earth’s corruption, matching the existing source tag.

review.translation: [And|0] [God|1] [looked at|0] [the earth|3,2], [and behold|4], [it had become corrupt|5], [because|6] [all|8] [flesh|9] [had corrupted|7] [its way|11,10] [on|12] [the earth|13].

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject, and אֶת־הָאָרֶץ marks the earth as the direct object of וַיַּרְא. The following וְהִנֵּה נִשְׁחָתָה describes what God saw when he looked at the earth: it was corrupt.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: In וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָרֶץ (“God saw the earth”), אֱלֹהִים is the subject of the third-person masculine singular verb וַיַּרְא. The singular agreement supports reading the plural form as referring to God.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural absolute common noun with singular verbal agreement.

analysis.evidence: In וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָרֶץ (‘God saw the earth’), אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיַּרְא, and אֶת marks הָאָרֶץ (‘the earth’) as its definite direct object.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֶת marks הָאָרֶץ as the object of וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים, “God saw the earth.” The feminine singular נִשְׁחָתָה describes the earth as corrupt, and כָּל־בָּשָׂר, “all flesh,” gives that judgment its worldwide scope.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ + common noun, singular absolute, with feminine agreement.

analysis.evidence: After וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת הָאָרֶץ (“God saw the earth”), וְהִנֵּה introduces what God saw. The following נִשְׁחָתָה describes the earth’s condition (“it was corrupt”).
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to the presentative particle הִנֵּה.
analysis.sense: and there was (what one sees or finds)

analysis.evidence: God sees that the earth (הָאָרֶץ) had become corrupt. The כִּי clause explains this by repeating the root שחת in the Hiphil: all flesh had corrupted its way (דַּרְכּוֹ). The reference to conduct gives נִשְׁחָתָה its moral sense.
analysis.morphology: Niphal perfect, third-person feminine singular, agreeing with הָאָרֶץ.

analysis.evidence: וְהִנֵּה נִשְׁחָתָה states that the earth was corrupt. כִּי introduces the reason for that condition, expressed by the related verb הִשְׁחִית: all flesh had corrupted its way on the earth.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected causal conjunction with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The collective singular subject כָּל בָּשָׂר, “all flesh,” governs הִשְׁחִית. The direct object אֶת דַּרְכּוֹ, “its way,” identifies what all flesh had corrupted: its own conduct.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil perfect, third person masculine singular, no prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: כָּל modifies the collective noun בָּשָׂר. Together they form the subject of הִשְׁחִית in the clause “all flesh had corrupted its way on the earth.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state.

analysis.evidence: כָּל בָּשָׂר is the collective subject of הִשְׁחִית, “had corrupted.” The singular suffix in דַּרְכּוֹ, “its way,” refers back to all flesh and describes the conduct of those living on the earth.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: all flesh: every living creature; mankind

analysis.evidence: In הִשְׁחִית כָּל בָּשָׂר אֶת דַּרְכּוֹ, “all flesh had corrupted its way,” כָּל בָּשָׂר is the subject of הִשְׁחִית. The marked אֶת introduces the direct object דַּרְכּוֹ, “its way,” which is definite through its possessive suffix.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected direct-object particle in the short form אֶת, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: אֶת marks דַּרְכּוֹ as the object of הִשְׁחִית ‘corrupted’. The suffix ־וֹ refers to the collective כָּל־בָּשָׂר ‘all flesh’. All flesh had corrupted the way it lived on earth.
analysis.morphology: Common-gender singular noun in the construct state with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix.

analysis.evidence: עַל takes הָאָרֶץ as its object. The phrase עַל הָאָרֶץ means “on the earth” and locates the conduct described in the clause.

The closing phrase עַל הָאָרֶץ means “on the earth.” It identifies the earth as the setting where כָּל בָּשָׂר (“all flesh”) had corrupted its way. The earlier mention of the same earth takes the feminine singular verb נִשְׁחָתָה.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ + common noun, singular absolute, common gender (feminine in this verse).
